examples.en: On Seollal we make tteokguk with garaetteok.

examples.ko: 갓 뽑은 가래떡을 조청에 찍어 먹었어요.
examples.en: I dipped freshly made garaetteok in grain syrup and ate it.

examples.ko: 가래떡을 얇게 썰어서 국에 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please slice the garaetteok thin and put it in the soup.
Garaetteok is chewy when you eat it while it's warm.

examples.ko: 우리 가래떡 구워서 꿀에 찍어 먹을까요?
examples.en: Shall we grill the garaetteok and dip it in honey?

examples.ko: 가래떡의 가운데를 뚝 잘라 친구와 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: I cut the garaetteok in the middle and shared it with my friend.

explain: 길쭉하고 흰 떡이에요. 얇게 썰어서 떡국에 넣거나, 구워서 꿀이나 조청에 찍어 먹어요. 설날 음식으로 많이 떠올려요.

phrases.en: I grill garaetteok and dip it in honey.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가래떡을 구워 먹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when grilling garaetteok to eat.

phrases.en: I sliced the garaetteok thinly to make tteokguk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떡국에 넣으려고 자를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cutting it for tteokguk.

phrases.en: I bought garaetteok for tteokguk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '용'을 붙여 쓰임새를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '용' to say what it is meant for.

explain_en: It is a long, white rice cake. People slice it thin for tteokguk, or grill it and dip it in honey or grain syrup. Many Koreans think of it as a Seollal food.

examples.en: I drank an energy drink the day before the exam.
This shop has many kinds of drinks.

examples.ko: 드링크 한 병을 마시고 힘을 냈어요.
examples.en: I drank a bottle of energy drink and got my energy up.
On my way home I bought a vitamin drink at the convenience store.
A drink is included in this set.
On the cafe menu, the drinks are on the right.

explain: 한국에서 '드링크'라고 하면 작은 병에 든 피로회복 음료를 떠올리는 사람이 많아요. 일반적으로 마시는 건 '음료'나 '음료수'라고 하고, 카페에서는 '커피', '차'처럼 종류로 말해요. 메뉴판에 '드링크'가 따로 있으면 음료 목록이라는 뜻이에요.

phrases.en: One bottle of a soft drink, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일반적으로 마시는 음료는 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for drinks in general.

phrases.en: I was tired, so I drank a fatigue-recovery drink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 병에 든 피로회복 음료를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small bottled drink for relieving tiredness.

phrases.en: Do you want a bottle of energy drink?
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 든 음료는 '병'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Bottled drinks are counted with 병.

explain_en: Small bottled health or energy drink, loanword. In Korea 드링크 makes many people think of a small bottled energy or recovery drink. Ordinary drinks are 음료 or 음료수, and at cafes people name the type, like 커피 or 차. A separate '드링크' section on a menu is the list of beverages.

dis.h: bottled energy or health tonic drink
gh: general word for any drinkable beverage

p.n: 음료 loses the sense of a tonic or energy drink and just means some beverage.

examples.en: I mix the seasoned greens with a little perilla oil.
The nutty smell of perilla oil whets my appetite.

examples.ko: 들기름은 냉장고에 두고 쓰는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to keep perilla oil in the fridge.
I brushed the seaweed with perilla oil and roasted it.
I tried perilla oil noodles for the first time.
I bought a bottle of perilla oil at the market.

explain: 들깨로 짠 기름이에요. 참깨로 짠 '참기름'과 향과 맛이 달라서 요리에서 서로 바꿔 쓰면 맛이 많이 달라져요. 나물, 김, 국수에 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I coat the pan with perilla oil and fry the tofu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름을 팬에 얇게 붓는 요리 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cooking phrase for thinly pouring oil in a pan.

phrases.en: I add one spoonful of perilla oil to the noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 넣는 양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tells the amount you add when cooking.

phrases.en: I put sesame oil in bibimbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참깨로 만든 기름이고 들기름과 향이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Oil made from sesame seeds, with a different aroma from 들기름.

explain_en: It is oil pressed from perilla seeds. It tastes and smells different from '참기름' (sesame oil), so swapping them changes a dish a lot. It is often used on namul, seaweed and noodles.

en: water kimchi; kimchi in a light brine

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 시원한 물김치가 입맛을 살려 줘요.
examples.en: On hot days, cool mulgimchi brings back your appetite.

examples.ko: 국수에 물김치 국물을 부어 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Noodles taste good with mulgimchi broth poured over them.

examples.ko: 할머니가 직접 담근 물김치를 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother sent me mulgimchi she made herself.

examples.ko: 물김치는 냉장고에서 하루 더 익혀야 맛있어요.
examples.en: Mulgimchi tastes better after ripening one more day in the fridge.

examples.ko: 이 물김치에 배와 무가 들어가서 달콤해요.
examples.en: Pear and radish go into this mulgimchi, so it's sweet.

examples.ko: 물김치만 있어도 밥 한 그릇이 뚝딱이에요.
examples.en: With just mulgimchi, a bowl of rice disappears in no time.

explain: 국물이 넉넉한 김치라서 건더기와 국물을 함께 먹어요. 동치미도 물김치의 한 종류예요. 매운 배추김치와 달리 맑고 시원한 맛이 특징이에요.

phrases.en: My mom makes mulgimchi every summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김치를 만들 때는 '담그다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '담그다' for making kimchi.

phrases.en: I eat noodles in mulgimchi broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건더기 말고 시원한 국물만 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to point to the cool broth, not the vegetables.

phrases.en: On hot days, cool mulgimchi is the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시원한'은 물김치의 맑고 차가운 맛을 말할 때 자주 붙어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '시원한' often goes with mulgimchi for its clear, cool taste.

explain_en: It is kimchi with plenty of broth, so you eat the vegetables and liquid together. Dongchimi is also a kind of mulgimchi. Unlike spicy cabbage kimchi, it is known for a clear, refreshing taste.

examples.en: This bread is made from wheat.
The wheat in the field has ripened yellow.
I have a wheat allergy.
Korea imports most of its wheat.

examples.ko: 쌀 대신 밀을 먹는 나라도 많아요.
examples.en: Many countries eat wheat instead of rice.
The price of wheat went up this year.

explain: 밀을 갈면 '밀가루'가 돼요. '밀'은 '밀다'의 어간과 소리가 같지만 다른 말이라서 문장에서 구별해요. 빵, 국수, 수제비의 재료예요.

phrases.en: We make bread and noodles from wheat flour.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀'을 갈아 만든 가루예요. 요리에서는 '밀'보다 '밀가루'를 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Flour ground from wheat; more common in cooking than plain '밀'.

phrases.en: I can see a wide wheat field outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밀을 키우는 밭을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A field where wheat is grown.

phrases.en: My grandfather grows wheat in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농사를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation when talking about farming.

explain_en: When wheat is ground it becomes '밀가루', flour. The noun '밀' sounds the same as the stem of the verb '밀다' (to push), but they are different words, so tell them apart in the sentence. It is the ingredient in bread, noodles and sujebi.

examples.ko: 날이 더워서 아이스티 한 잔 시켰어요.
examples.en: It was hot, so I ordered an iced tea.
I put a slice of lemon in my iced tea.
I drink iced tea instead of coffee.

examples.ko: 아이스티가 너무 달아서 물을 조금 더 탔어요.
examples.en: The iced tea was too sweet, so I added a little more water.

examples.ko: 편의점에서 캔 아이스티를 두 개 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two cans of iced tea at the convenience store.
Have you ever made iced tea at home yourself?

explain: 카페에서는 '아이스'와 '핫'으로 나눠서 주문해요. 가루를 물에 타서 마시는 복숭아 맛 음료도 보통 '아이스티'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I'll have one iced tea, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카페에서 주문할 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to order it at a cafe.

phrases.example: 더운 날에는 레몬 아이스티가 시원해서 좋아요.
phrases.en: On hot days, lemon iced tea is nice and refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛이나 종류를 붙여서 메뉴 이름처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding a flavor makes it sound like a menu item.

phrases.en: I made iced tea from powder and drank it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가루를 물에 풀어 직접 만들 때 '타다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'tada' (to mix) when you make it yourself from powder in water.

explain_en: At cafés you order either 'ice' or 'hot'. A peach-flavored drink made by mixing powder with water is also commonly called '아이스티'.

examples.en: Grandmother took a hard candy out of her pocket and gave it to me.

examples.ko: 알사탕을 입에 물고 있으면 볼이 볼록해져요.
examples.en: When you hold a round candy in your mouth, your cheek bulges.

examples.ko: 아이가 알사탕 하나에 금방 기분이 풀렸어요.
examples.en: The child cheered up right away with just one candy.

examples.ko: 알사탕은 오래 녹여 먹을 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like round candies because you can enjoy them for a long time.
I bought three round candies at the stationery store.

examples.ko: 알사탕이 너무 커서 한 번에 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: The candy is so big that I can't eat it all at once.

explain: '사탕' 중에서도 동글동글한 알 모양의 딱딱한 사탕을 가리켜요. 막대 모양 사탕과 구별해서 말할 때 쓰고, 보통 깨물지 않고 입에서 녹여 먹어요.

phrases.en: Please give me just one hard candy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동글동글한 사탕을 셀 때 '알'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'al' to count round candies.

phrases.en: I slowly let the candy melt in my mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨물지 않고 입에서 녹이는 먹는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the way of eating it by dissolving, not biting.
phrases.en_equiv: to let a candy melt in one's mouth

phrases.en: My little brother fell asleep with a candy in his mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사탕을 입에 넣고 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes keeping the candy in one's mouth.
phrases.en_equiv: to hold a candy in one's mouth

explain_en: Among '사탕' (candy), it specifically means the hard, round, ball-shaped kind. It is used to tell it apart from lollipop-type candy, and people usually let it dissolve in the mouth instead of biting it.

examples.en: I ordered omelette rice for lunch.
I drew a heart on the omelette rice with ketchup.
This restaurant is famous for its delicious omelette rice.

examples.ko: 오므라이스는 계란을 얇게 부쳐서 싸야 해요.
examples.en: For omelette rice, you need to fry the egg thin and wrap it.
I tried omelette rice with curry on top.
I can't decide between omelette rice and pork cutlet.

explain: 볶음밥을 달걀로 감싼 요리라서 달걀이 위에 올라간 일반 볶음밥과 달라요. 식당 메뉴 이름으로 자주 보이고, 케첩이나 소스를 얹어서 먹어요. 철자는 '오무라이스'가 아니라 '오므라이스'예요.

phrases.en: I'll order the omelette rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 메뉴를 고를 때 '시키다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '시키다' when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.en: One plate of omelette rice, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 수를 말해 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the quantity when ordering.

phrases.en: This place is known for great omelette rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 음식을 잘하는 식당을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a restaurant that is good at that dish.

explain_en: It is fried rice wrapped in egg, so it differs from plain fried rice with an egg on top. You often see it on restaurant menus, usually with ketchup or sauce. The spelling is '오므라이스', not '오무라이스'.

en: born in the Year of the Dog

examples.en: I was born in the year of the dog, and my older brother was born in the year of the horse.
People born in the year of the dog gathered.
This meeting is only for people born in the year of the dog.
I was glad to meet someone with the same zodiac sign, the dog.
Are you born in the year of the dog? I didn't know.

examples.ko: 개띠는 열두 띠 중에서 열한 번째예요.
examples.en: The dog is the eleventh of the twelve zodiac animals.

explain: 태어난 해의 동물로 말하는 열두 띠 중 개예요. 한국에서는 나이를 물을 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 묻기도 해요. '말띠', '용띠'처럼 '동물+띠'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I was born in the year of the dog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 띠를 말할 때 '~띠예요'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say '~띠예요' to tell your zodiac animal.

phrases.en: What's your zodiac animal? I'm a dog.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 띠나 나이를 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone's zodiac animal, or indirectly their age.

phrases.en: This is a friend born in the same dog year as me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 해에 태어난 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone born in the same year.
phrases.en_equiv: a friend born in the dog year

explain_en: It is the dog in the twelve zodiac animals, based on the year you were born. In Korea people sometimes ask about age with '무슨 띠예요?'. Other signs are said as 'animal + 띠', like '말띠' and '용띠'.

en: born in the year of the Snake; Snake zodiac sign

examples.ko: 제 동생은 이천일 년에 태어나서 뱀띠예요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was born in 2001, so they were born in the year of the snake.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지와 저는 둘 다 뱀띠예요.
examples.en: My father and I are both born in the year of the snake.

examples.ko: 뱀띠 친구와 같이 생일 파티를 했어요.
examples.en: I had a birthday party together with a friend born in the year of the snake.

examples.ko: 뱀띠 해는 십이 년마다 한 번씩 돌아와요.
examples.en: The year of the snake comes around once every twelve years.
When people ask 'What is your zodiac sign?', I answer 'I'm a snake.'

examples.ko: 우리 반에서 뱀띠인 사람은 몇 명이에요?
examples.en: How many people in our class were born in the year of the snake?

explain: 태어난 해에 따라 정해지는 열두 동물 띠 중에서 뱀의 해에 태어난 사람을 말해요. 한국에서는 나이를 직접 묻기 어려울 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 묻기도 해요. '뱀띠 해'처럼 그 해 자체를 가리킬 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: Many people were born in the year of the snake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 뱀의 해라는 그 해 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the year of the snake itself, not the person.

phrases.example: 뱀띠인 친구가 저보다 한 살 많아요.
phrases.en: My friend who was born in the year of the snake is one year older than me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족이 어떤 띠인지 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which zodiac sign a friend or family member has.
phrases.en_equiv: a friend born in the year of the snake

phrases.en: What is your zodiac animal? I'm a snake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띠를 물어볼 때 쓰는 말이고, 대답할 때 '뱀띠예요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The question for asking someone's zodiac animal; answer with '뱀띠예요'.

explain_en: It refers to a person born in a year of the snake, one of the twelve zodiac animals. In Korea people sometimes ask '무슨 띠예요?' when it is awkward to ask age directly. It can also point to the year itself, as in '뱀띠 해'.

examples.en: On Christmas I eat cake with my family.
As Christmas approaches, the streets sparkle.
Christmas is on December 25.
For Christmas we sang songs at church.
I haven't bought a Christmas gift yet.
This year Christmas is also a holiday, so I'm going on a trip.

explain: '크리스마스'와 같은 날이지만, 뉴스나 안내문 같은 글에서는 '성탄절'이라고도 써요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '크리스마스'를 더 많이 말해요. 한국에서는 12월 25일이 공휴일이에요.

phrases.en: On Christmas, I have a party with friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성탄절과 같은 날이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '크리스마스'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same day as 성탄절. In everyday talk, 크리스마스 is more common.

phrases.en: I gave my parents a Christmas present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성탄절에 주고받는 선물이에요. 글이나 안내문에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gift exchanged at Christmas; natural in writing and notices.

phrases.example: 성탄절 연휴에 가족과 여행을 갈 거예요.
phrases.en: I will travel with my family over the Christmas holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성탄절 앞뒤로 쉬는 며칠을 말해요. 공휴일이 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The few days off around Christmas, when holidays run together.

explain_en: Formal native-Sino word; official calendars, greetings, churches. It is the same day as '크리스마스', but news and notices also write '성탄절'. With friends, people tend to say '크리스마스'. December 25 is a public holiday in Korea.

en: born in the Year of the Ox; Ox zodiac sign

examples.en: I was born in the year of the ox and my brother in the year of the tiger.

examples.ko: 소띠 사람들은 성실하다는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: People born in the year of the ox often hear that they are diligent.
My mother was born in 1961, the year of the ox.

examples.ko: 올해 소띠 운세를 보고 싶어서 앱을 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened an app because I wanted to check this year's fortune for the ox sign.

examples.ko: 친구랑 제가 둘 다 소띠인 걸 오늘 알았어요.
examples.en: I found out today that my friend and I are both ox-year people.
Please recommend a gift that suits someone born in the year of the ox.

explain: '띠'는 태어난 해를 열두 동물로 나타낸 거예요. 한국에서는 나이를 물을 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 묻기도 해요. 같은 띠끼리는 열두 살 차이가 나고, 이를 '띠동갑'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My husband was born in the year of the ox.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무슨 띠예요?'라는 질문에 이렇게 대답해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is how you answer the question '무슨 띠예요?'.

phrases.en: I was born in the year of the ox.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태어난 해를 조금 길게 풀어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly longer way to say the year you were born.
phrases.en_equiv: to be born in the year of the ox

phrases.en: What's your zodiac animal? I'm an ox.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이를 간접적으로 물을 때 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sometimes used to ask about age indirectly.

explain_en: '띠' shows the year of your birth through one of twelve animals. In Korea, people sometimes ask '무슨 띠예요?' as a way of asking about age. People of the same animal are twelve years apart, which is called '띠동갑'.

examples.ko: 식목일에 가족과 함께 산에서 나무를 심었어요.
examples.en: On Arbor Day, I planted trees in the mountains with my family.
Arbor Day is April 5th every year.

examples.ko: 식목일 행사로 공원에 묘목을 심으러 갔어요.
examples.en: For the Arbor Day event, I went to plant saplings in the park.
Tomorrow is Arbor Day, so I will plant trees with the kids.
Where do you go to plant trees on Arbor Day?

examples.ko: 올해 식목일에는 비가 와서 행사가 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: It rained this Arbor Day, so the event was postponed.

explain: '식목'은 나무를 심는다는 한자어라 보통 '식목일'로만 나와요. 일상에서 나무를 심는 일은 그냥 '나무를 심다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The school held an Arbor Day event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식목일에 열리는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An event held on Arbor Day.

phrases.en: When Arbor Day comes near, we go to plant trees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날이 가까워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the day is getting close.

phrases.en: I got up early on the morning of Arbor Day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날의 시간대를 붙여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a time of day to the date.

explain_en: '식목' is a Sino-Korean word for planting trees and mostly appears only in '식목일'. In everyday speech, planting trees is simply '나무를 심다'.
